summary: Fail2ban-style brute-force protection.
evidence: No fail2ban integration in dev. Closest pieces: per-endpoint rate limit (ratelimit.go), WAF (Coraza/CRS), access blacklist; logs are plain text under the log folder so external fail2ban/CrowdSec can read them (see #578, #648). Roadmap sections 1 (admin login lockout) and 9 (structured JSON access logs) are the right vehicles. Value M, effort M (login lockout S, auto-ban from 401/403 counts M).

summary: Forward authentication (Authelia/Authentik/Keycloak style) in the UI.
evidence: AuthMethodForward in src/mod/dynamicproxy/authProviders.go (handleForwardAuth), generic forward auth module src/mod/auth/sso/forward, Authentik presets + OIDC in the fork (mod/auth/sso/forward/authentik_test.go, docs/authentik.md; ROADMAP section 4). Not verified against a real Authentik (fork issue #213).
proposed_comment: Forward auth is available in the HTTP proxy rule editor (Authentication provider -> Forward Auth), including Authentik presets and OIDC on this fork (see `docs/authentik.md`). Closing; open specific bugs separately.

summary: Multiple admin accounts for the management UI.
evidence: Admin auth is a single user (src/mod/auth). ZorxAuth (site SSO) has multiple users but that is for proxied sites, not the admin panel. Effort L (user model, roles, audit); maintainers' stance upstream was 'put an auth gateway in front'. With OIDC support now in the fork, an SSO-protected admin panel is the more realistic route. Value M, effort L.

summary: Built-in Zrok support (like ZeroTier).
evidence: Not present. Zrok can be run as a sidecar/plugin that exposes a local port. Better suited to the plugin system than core. Value low, effort M.

summary: Simplified Chinese UI.
evidence: No i18n framework in the admin UI (strings hard-coded in src/web/*.html). Tied to #236. Value M, effort L (extract strings, translation files, language switch).

summary: Cluster / HA capability.
evidence: Maps to ROADMAP section 6 (config sync, stateless sessions, certificate sync, keepalived guide). Already partly done in the fork: stateless CAPTCHA sessions. Cluster work is in flight elsewhere, so not touched. Interim answer from upstream thread: run two nodes with the same config and keepalived/VRRP.

summary: Multi-language UI.
evidence: Same as #166: no i18n layer. Value M, effort L.

summary: Restrict access to a sub path (e.g. /admin LAN only).
evidence: Access rules attach to a whole host endpoint (runEndpointChain in src/mod/dynamicproxy/Server.go), not to a vdir/path. Basic auth has path/CIDR exception rules but no path-scoped allow list. Related fork roadmap item: per-path rate limits (section 1) and WAF path-scoped rules (WAF custom SecLang can already deny a path from non-LAN IPs: SecRule REQUEST_URI "@beginsWith /admin" chained with REMOTE_ADDR !@ipMatch ...). Value H, effort M.

summary: Challenge (CAPTCHA) instead of block for selected countries.
evidence: GeoIP block/allow exists; the fork has per-endpoint CAPTCHA with customisable pages (roadmap section 3, fork #77) but no 'challenge when country is X' action. Reasonable small addition: add a country list to the CAPTCHA trigger. Value M, effort M.

summary: Global error pages for upstream status codes (proxy_intercept_errors).
evidence: Only the default-site 404 template (<webroot>/templates/notfound.html) and the host error page are customisable; upstream error status codes are passed through. Value M, effort M.

summary: Odoo websocket (/websocket on port 8072) fails behind a virtual directory.
evidence: Virtual directories strip the matching prefix before forwarding (rewriteURL in src/mod/dynamicproxy/proxyRequestHandler.go), so a vdir '/websocket' -> http://odoochat:8072 reaches Odoo as '/' not '/websocket' (nginx's proxy_pass without URI keeps the path). Unverified here (no Odoo). Suggested reply below.
proposed_comment: Zoraxy strips the vdir prefix, unlike `proxy_pass http://odoochat;`. Try giving the virtual directory `/websocket` the target `odoochat-host:8072/websocket` (include the path in the target) so the prefix is re-added upstream. Also make sure the proxied host keeps the original Host header and that Odoo has `proxy_mode = True`. If that still fails please post the websocket request/response headers.

summary: Route 53 DNS challenge: 'cannot unmarshal string into Config.MaxRetries of type int'.
evidence: UI builds int fields from number inputs (class typeint in src/web/snippet/acme.html readDnsCredentials, parseInt) so the payload carries a JSON number. Test mod/acme/acme_dns_int_test.go (commit 583fb4d) shows numeric MaxRetries accepted and a string value still produces the quoted error, i.e. only a payload from an old UI/stale saved credentials can trigger it. Residual: credentials saved by an old UI keep the string; re-save them.
proposed_comment: Fixed: the ACME UI now sends integer provider fields (e.g. `MaxRetries`) as JSON numbers; covered by `TestRoute53IntCredentialFieldsAccepted`. If you saved Route 53 credentials with an old version, re-enter and save them once.

summary: Filter statistics per site.
evidence: Statistics are global (src/mod/statistic, analytic loader). The data model keeps per-host maps so a host filter is feasible. Overlaps #764 and #596. Value M, effort M.

summary: Exclude own IP from statistics.
evidence: No ignore list in statistic.RecordRequest. Value M, effort S (ignore CIDR list option in the collector).

summary: Source IP lost when forwarding SMTP via TCP stream proxy.
evidence: Stream proxy supports PROXY protocol v1/v2 (ProxyProtocolV1/V2 in src/mod/streamproxy/streamproxy.go), which is exactly the answer for mail. Backend (Proxmox Mail Gateway/Postfix postscreen) must be configured to accept it.
proposed_comment: Enable **PROXY protocol** (v1 or v2) on the TCP proxy rule and configure the receiving MTA to expect it (Postfix: `postscreen_upstream_proxy_protocol = haproxy`). A plain TCP stream always shows Zoraxy's own IP as source, headers like X-Forwarded-For do not exist for SMTP.

summary: Serve Lua scripts instead of a backend.
evidence: Out of scope for core; plugin territory (fork roadmap section 8). Value low, effort L.

summary: Variables/aliases (e.g. {{external_ip}}) in rules.
evidence: Not present. Low value; the same need is met by trusted-proxy lists and access rules. Effort M.

summary: Disable weak (CBC-SHA1/3DES) ciphers.
evidence: TLS cipher profile setting (Global settings -> TLS cipher profile; src/mod/dynamicproxy/tlscipherprofile.go, tests tlscipherprofile_test.go): 'intermediate' removes CBC-SHA1 suites, 'modern' is TLS 1.3 only. 3DES is already disabled in Go.
proposed_comment: Available now: System Settings -> TLS cipher profile (`intermediate` = Mozilla intermediate AEAD-only TLS 1.2 suites, `modern` = TLS 1.3 only). Closing.

summary: Pre-select DNS challenge when creating a proxy rule.
evidence: UI-only convenience: new-rule flow calls obtainCertificate(..., dns=false) in web/components/rules.html. Value L-M, effort S.

summary: REST API to list/create proxy records.
evidence: Internal /api/* endpoints exist but are cookie+CSRF authenticated for the UI; plugins have API keys (ROADMAP section 8). A documented token-based API would be new. Related fork roadmap: Swagger docs (fork #197 mirrors upstream). Value H, effort M.

summary: ACME HTTP-01 gets 404 (Docker, DDNS domain).
evidence: A 404 for /.well-known/acme-challenge/<token> means the request did not reach Zoraxy's ACME relay (another service on port 80, router forwarding port 80 elsewhere) or Zoraxy was not listening on 80. dev fixes one real cause (c0d317e: host with a proxy rule + plain-HTTP listener returned 400 for challenges). Cannot verify reporter's network.
proposed_comment: A 404 from Let's Encrypt means the challenge request was answered by something other than Zoraxy. Check that external port 80 is forwarded to the Zoraxy container's port 80 (and that 'Enable HTTP server on port 80' is on), and that no other service (NAS web server, router UI) answers on 80. Test with `curl -v http://yourdomain/.well-known/acme-challenge/test` from outside; it should return 400/404 from Zoraxy, not a foreign page. If the domain also has an AAAA record make sure IPv6 reaches Zoraxy as well.

summary: Uptime Kuma intermittently reports ECONNREFUSED / 'unable to verify the first certificate'.
evidence: 'unable to verify the first certificate' is the classic missing-intermediate-chain symptom: the served PEM must contain leaf + chain (Zoraxy serves the uploaded file as is). ECONNREFUSED comes from upstream/Docker networking. Not reproducible without the reporter's environment.

summary: Staging ACME provider.
evidence: A global flag -acmetestmode switches every CA to its staging URL (src/def.go, src/mod/acme/ca.json 'Test' map), but there is no per-request toggle in the UI. Value M, effort S.

summary: Hurricane Electric (he.net) DNS provider.
evidence: lego v5.5.2 ships dns/hurricane but it is absent from src/mod/acme/acmedns/providers.json and acmedns.go; its Config uses Credentials map[string]string (domain -> 'user:token'), which the generated key/value form cannot express. Needs a map-type field in the form and the code generator. Value L-M, effort M.

summary: How to proxy only /api, /local, /media of a host (nginx location regex).
evidence: Virtual directories are prefix based, one per path. Default behaviour is that the host's own target handles everything else, so the 'other directories stop working' point suggests the proxy rule root target is missing/wrong rather than a Zoraxy limitation.
proposed_comment: Set the host rule's target to Home Assistant (`homeassistant:8123`); that already serves `/lovelace`, `/api`, `/local`, `/media` and everything else. Virtual directories are only needed to send a *path* to a *different* upstream. Create the three vdirs only if they must go elsewhere, one per prefix (no regex alternation).

summary: Static files 404 when an app is mounted under a virtual directory /app/.
evidence: Vdir strips the prefix (rewriteURL) but the app emits absolute links (/css/...). Zoraxy does not rewrite response bodies; the app must be configured with a base URL/path or be given its own sub-domain.
proposed_comment: Zoraxy forwards `/app/x` to the container as `/x` and does not rewrite HTML. If the app emits root-relative URLs (`/css/style.css`) the browser requests them without `/app`. Either set the app's base-URL/path option, or use a dedicated sub-domain (`app.example.com`) instead of a virtual directory.

summary: robots.txt / static response per host or vdir.
evidence: No static-response endpoint; closest is default-site templates. Could be a 'static response' vdir type or a WAF/response rule. Value M, effort S-M.

summary: Generate CSR in the UI.
evidence: Not present (tlscert generates self-signed certs only). Value low, effort S-M (crypto/x509.CreateCertificateRequest).

summary: Mutual TLS (client certificate auth).
evidence: Not implemented for proxy endpoints (tls.Config ClientAuth not set; only appears in cert generation). Needs per-host CA upload + tls.Config GetConfigForClient. Highly requested upstream. Value H, effort M-L.

summary: Domoticz/OctoPrint resources return 404 behind Zoraxy.
evidence: Same pattern as #418: sub-path (vdir) mounting with root-relative asset URLs. Reporter said no special rules, so more info (rule screenshot) needed.
proposed_comment: Please post the HTTP proxy rule and virtual directory configuration. If these apps are mounted under a path (e.g. `/domoticz`) the vdir prefix is stripped and absolute asset links break; serve them on their own sub-domain, or set the app's base path.

summary: Punycode (IDN) domain fails with Infomaniak DNS challenge ('domain not found eu').
evidence: Error comes from lego's Infomaniak provider zone lookup for the xn-- name (Infomaniak API appears to expect the Unicode form or the registered zone). Needs an Infomaniak account to reproduce; the fix might be passing the Unicode name to that provider only.

summary: Certificate shows 'Unknown' expiry when the PEM starts with a PUBLIC KEY block.
evidence: Real bug: handler.go only decoded the FIRST PEM block, so any bundle where block 1 is not a CERTIFICATE (public key first, key first, ...) lost expiry/domain. Added firstCertificate() in src/mod/tlscert/helper.go (skips non-certificate blocks) used by the 3 listing sites; test mod/tlscert/firstcert_test.go (failed to build before, passes now).
proposed_comment: Fixed on the fork (a00613f): the certificate list now scans all PEM blocks and uses the first CERTIFICATE one, so bundles that start with a PUBLIC KEY block show the right expiry date and domain. Test: `TestFirstCertificateSkipsLeadingNonCertBlocks`.

summary: Prometheus metrics endpoint.
evidence: Not present; ROADMAP section 9 (planned). Value H, effort M. #660 asks for the same.

summary: ACME fails (403) once any proxy rule has 'Allow plain HTTP access'.
evidence: Root cause was the non-TLS path (port 80 bypass) skipping the special routing rules, so challenges were proxied to the backend (403). Fixed in dev by d3add94 (shared pre-proxy chain; handleNonTLSRequest calls handleSpecialAndRedirect); test TestNonTLS_SpecialRoutingRuleApplies. Additionally c0d317e fixes the sibling case from the same thread (host has a rule, no plain-HTTP bypass, 'force HTTPS redirect' off -> port 80 returned 400 for challenges): handlePort80Request now answers ACME rules first; test TestPort80ServesACMEChallengeForExistingProxyRule fails without the change.
proposed_comment: Fixed on the fork: plain-HTTP endpoints now go through the same special routing (ACME) as HTTPS ones (d3add94, test `TestNonTLS_SpecialRoutingRuleApplies`), and the port-80 listener answers ACME HTTP-01 challenges for any host with a proxy rule (c0d317e, test `TestPort80ServesACMEChallengeForExistingProxyRule`).

summary: How to update a bare-metal Zoraxy.
evidence: The fork has an in-app updater (System -> Update, DEVELOPMENT.md 'Updating / releasing'); for the source install: git pull, rebuild in src/ (go build), restart; the reporter built in the right place so 'no newer version' simply means their checkout was already current.
proposed_comment: On this fork use **System -> Update** (checks signed GitHub releases, one click install with rollback). For a source checkout: back up `conf/` and `sys.db`, `git pull`, `cd src && go build`, restart the service. Docker: pull the new image.

summary: Hooks after certificate renewal.
evidence: Not present (renewal in src/mod/acme/autorenew.go). Value M, effort S (run configured command/webhook after a successful renew).

summary: Change the admin username.
evidence: Username is fixed at first-run setup; only the password can be changed (src/mod/auth). Value L, effort S (add field + migration of the stored hash key). Workaround: edit the database.

summary: IPv6 calculator in the toolbox.
evidence: Only IPv4 calculator exists (web/components/utils.html). Pure front-end task. Value low, effort S.

summary: Bulk import IPs/CIDRs into the blacklist.
evidence: Trusted-proxy list has a CSV bulk import (handleBulkUpdateTrustedProxies in accesslist.go) but the blacklist/whitelist editors do not. Same ask as #661, fork issue #211. Value H, effort S.

summary: Let's Encrypt validates over IPv6 (AAAA) and hits a different server.
evidence: LE prefers IPv6 when an AAAA record exists; Zoraxy does not control which family LE uses and cannot force the challenge client to IPv4. The 403 shows the AAAA address answering.
proposed_comment: Let's Encrypt chooses the address family itself: if the name has an AAAA record, validation goes to that IPv6 address (here a backend server, hence 403). Either remove the AAAA record for names Zoraxy must obtain certs for, forward IPv6 port 80/443 to Zoraxy too, or use the DNS challenge, which does not depend on reachability.

summary: Backend sees Zoraxy's IP instead of the client IP.
evidence: Zoraxy sets X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-Ip on proxied requests; backends must be told to trust the proxy (Authelia: trusted proxies / X-Forwarded-For). If Zoraxy itself sits behind another hop, add that hop to Trusted proxies.
proposed_comment: Zoraxy already sends `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Real-Ip`. The backend (Authelia here) must be configured to trust Zoraxy's address (`server.endpoints.authz.*.implementation: ForwardAuth` + trusted proxy list) and read the client IP from those headers. The TCP source address is always Zoraxy's in an HTTP reverse proxy.

summary: Allow SMTP without authentication.
evidence: email.go SendEmail already skips auth when the password is empty (smtp.SendMail with nil auth), and in dev nothing calls NewEmailSender (no 'forgot password' UI wired). Nothing to change/verify here.
proposed_comment: In the current code the mail sender sends without AUTH when no password is set, but the reset-by-email flow is not wired into the UI on this fork. Please re-open as a feature request if you still need it.

summary: LE renewal error 400 'Error getting validation data'.
evidence: LE reports it could not fetch the challenge from the host, i.e. reachability/DNS (CNAME to DDNS, IPv6, port 80 forwarding). One genuine Zoraxy cause is fixed by c0d317e (port 80 answered 400 for hosts with a proxy rule and no redirect) but the thread has no evidence this is the reporter's case.
proposed_comment: That error is raised by Let's Encrypt, not Zoraxy: it could not fetch `http://<host>/.well-known/acme-challenge/...`. Check port 80 forwarding, the CNAME/DDNS target and any AAAA record. Recent fork builds also fix the port-80 listener rejecting challenges for hosts with a proxy rule when 'force HTTPS redirect' is off (c0d317e); please retest.

summary: Certificate warning for a proxied Synology on macvlan.
evidence: Client-side name resolution/hairpin (macvlan shim, Pi-hole); if the browser reaches Zoraxy through a name/IP not covered by the certificate it gets the fallback cert. Not a Zoraxy defect.
proposed_comment: A browser warning with a valid cert means the request is being served with the fallback (self-signed) certificate, i.e. the hostname used did not match a proxy rule/cert (or SNI is missing because the client uses the IP). Verify that the local DNS record resolves the same name used in the proxy rule and open the exact hostname; `openssl s_client -connect ip:443 -servername host` shows which cert is served.

summary: Today's statistics lost on container restart.
evidence: NewStatisticCollector reloads today's summary from the database (src/mod/statistic/statistic.go), autosave every 10 min (STATISTIC_AUTO_SAVE_INTERVAL) and ShutdownSeq saves on SIGTERM/SIGINT (src/main.go). New test mod/statistic/restart_test.go: TestTodayStatsSurviveRestart passes (commit 1368039). Requires sys.db to be on a persistent volume.
proposed_comment: Today's totals are reloaded at startup, saved every 10 minutes and on SIGTERM; regression test `TestTodayStatsSurviveRestart`. Make sure `sys.db` lives on the mounted volume (`/opt/zoraxy/config`).

summary: Sablier (scale-to-zero) compatibility.
evidence: Plugin territory (upstream thread says a plugin is planned). Needs pre-request hook that waits for a container; ROADMAP section 8 hooks would enable it. Value L-M, effort M.

summary: Log requests answered by the default-site 404.
evidence: Deliberate: Server.go (default-site branch) says 'Do not log default site requests to avoid flooding the logs', and serve404PageWithTemplate does not log. Making it optional is small. Value M, effort S (setting 'log unmatched-host requests').

summary: Backend shows Zoraxy IP not public IP.
evidence: Same as #514/#676: HTTP reverse proxy sets forwarding headers; the backend must read them.
proposed_comment: Zoraxy sends `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Real-Ip`. Configure the backend service to trust the proxy and use those headers. If another firewall/NAT sits in front and masquerades the source, Zoraxy sees that device's IP: fix at the firewall (disable source NAT / use PROXY protocol).

summary: Separate log files per site.
evidence: Single log stream (src/mod/info/logger, rotation by month). Could add per-endpoint log file option. Overlaps #764 and ROADMAP section 9. Value M, effort M.

summary: 'Filename cannot be empty for certs containing multiple domains' when obtaining a cert for a host with aliases.
evidence: Real bug in web/components/cert.html obtainCertificate(): filename was hard-coded to '' so any comma-separated domain list (alias) always took the error branch. Now the file is named after the first domain. JS-only change: no automated test possible in this repo, logic checked by reading; UI not click-tested.
proposed_comment: Fixed on the fork (67036ea): requesting a certificate for a host with aliases now names the file after the primary domain instead of failing. Not click-tested in a browser; please confirm.

summary: Access rule blocks WireGuard clients (sees VPN server IP).
evidence: The client's source is whatever address reaches Zoraxy; WireGuard server masquerading (SNAT) hides the client. Trusted proxies only helps with HTTP headers.
proposed_comment: If the WireGuard server NATs (masquerades) client traffic, Zoraxy only ever sees the VPN server's IP. Disable masquerade for the LAN-bound traffic (route the VPN subnet instead of NAT-ing it) and then allow the VPN subnet in the access rule.

summary: Bot blocking (user-agent rules, known bad bot lists).
evidence: No UA rule UI. The fork WAF (Coraza + CRS, ROADMAP section 7) already includes scanner/bot detection rules and accepts custom SecLang (e.g. block a User-Agent) so a lot is possible via WAF; a UI list and a bundled bad-bot list would be new. Value M, effort M.

summary: Basic auth only for a virtual directory (/admin).
evidence: Basic auth is per host endpoint with exception paths (BasicAuthExceptionRules) but cannot be scoped to include only a path. Value M, effort M (per-vdir auth).

summary: Websocket 'bad handshake' to graphql backend.
evidence: Backend rejected the upgrade; upstream thread suggests config issue. Zoraxy forwards Upgrade headers and rewrites Origin for vdirs (proxyRequestHandler.go vdirRequest). A usual cause: vdir prefix stripping (/graphql -> /) or Origin/Host check on the backend. Cannot verify.
proposed_comment: 'bad handshake' = the backend answered the websocket Upgrade with something other than 101. Check the backend log for the response code. Likely causes: the vdir prefix is stripped so the path differs from what the app expects (include the path in the vdir target), or the app validates Origin/Host. Try 'Skip WebSocket Origin Check' on the rule.

summary: CrowdSec needs live logs.
evidence: HTTP access lines are written live to <logfolder>/zr_YYYY-M.log (src/mod/info/logger/logger.go); CrowdSec can tail that file with a custom acquisition + parser.
proposed_comment: Zoraxy writes request lines continuously to `log/zr_<year>-<month>.log` (one file per month; older months stay in the folder). Point a CrowdSec `file` acquisition at `log/zr_*.log`; a community parser/bouncer plugin exists (see the plugin list).

summary: Bypass forward-auth for server-to-server calls.
evidence: Real gap: Basic auth and ZorxAuth have exception rules (authProviders.go) but handleForwardAuth/OAuth2 have none. Add IP/CIDR and path exception rules to all providers. Value H, effort S-M.

summary: ACME relay logs 'connection refused' and answers 200 to scanner probes of /.well-known/acme-challenge/.
evidence: Real (minor) bugs: the relay (src/acme.go) printed Printf errors and wrote an empty 200 when no issuance was running and never passed through the internal listener's status. Extracted serveACMEChallenge: 404 when the internal listener is down, status passthrough, token regex rejects names like my1.php with 400 (that part was already fixed). Test src/acme_challenge_test.go. NOT fixed: the ACME routing rule has UseSystemAccessControl=false so blacklisted IPs can still reach it (harmless while the listener is closed).
proposed_comment: Partly fixed on the fork (45a5c89): the challenge relay now answers 404 quietly when no certificate request is running and passes the real status through. The 'errors' were scanner probes of the well-known path, not a leak. Leaving open: ACME path ignores the IP blacklist.

summary: Prometheus metrics.
evidence: Duplicate of #461.
proposed_comment: Duplicate of #461 (Prometheus metrics endpoint, ROADMAP section 9).

summary: Import IP blocklist (TXT).
evidence: Duplicate of #512 (bulk import of IPs/CIDRs into blacklist).
proposed_comment: Duplicate of #512 / fork #211 (bulk import for the blacklist).

summary: Proxy to unix socket.
evidence: Not present; dpcore transport could dial unix:// targets (DialContext). Upstream says plugin/non-Windows. Value M, effort M.

summary: Certificate error when hitting the default site by IP.
evidence: Answered in thread: the default site over HTTPS needs a fallback certificate that matches; IP access always warns because a cert cannot match an unknown host.
proposed_comment: That is expected: for requests by IP or unknown host Zoraxy serves the *fallback certificate* (self-signed unless you set one under TLS/SSL -> Set as fallback). A browser can only avoid the warning if the name used is covered by that certificate; a redirect is performed after the TLS handshake.

summary: Pass the real client IP instead of Cloudflare's.
evidence: Zoraxy passes X-Real-Ip/X-Forwarded-For; with Cloudflare, add Cloudflare ranges to Trusted proxies (web/components/trustedproxy.html, access/trustedProxy tests) so the CF-Connecting-IP value is used for access control and forwarded.
proposed_comment: Add the Cloudflare IP ranges under the **Trusted Proxy** page so Zoraxy takes the client IP from `CF-Connecting-IP`/`X-Forwarded-For`, then configure Home Assistant (`http: use_x_forwarded_for: true`, `trusted_proxies: <zoraxy ip>`).

summary: Load balance by client IP/region/CIDR.
evidence: Fork LB has IP hash and consistent hash (ROADMAP section 5, #79) but no GeoIP/CIDR routing. Value M, effort M (a 'geo' selection rule in loadbalance).

summary: Answer CORS preflight (OPTIONS) in the proxy.
evidence: Custom headers exist, but no way to answer OPTIONS at the proxy without hitting the upstream. A 'CORS' option per endpoint would cover it. Value M, effort S-M.

summary: How to configure PowerDNS provider (udmedia.de).
evidence: Provider 'pdns' exists in providers.json: needs API key + Host URL; optional fields may be left empty.
proposed_comment: Choose provider `pdns`. Fill **APIKey** and **Host** (your PowerDNS API base URL, e.g. `https://ns.example.org`) and leave the optional fields at their defaults; **ServerName** is usually `localhost`.

summary: Lookahead/lookbehind regex in redirect rules.
evidence: Redirect rules use Go RE2 (error 'invalid or unsupported Perl syntax: (?!'). regexp2 (MIT) could be used, with ReDoS/timeouts considered. Value L-M, effort S-M.

summary: Authentik forward auth gives redirect errors / 400.
evidence: Upstream feature has been reworked in the fork: Authentik forward auth uses the outpost callback path, server-built rd, Host preservation and X-authentik-* handling (ROADMAP 4, docs/authentik.md, src/mod/auth/sso/forward tests with fake outposts). Needs a real Authentik instance to confirm (fork issue #213).

summary: Simple API for proxy rules and ACLs.
evidence: Duplicate of #382 (REST API to manage proxy records).
proposed_comment: Duplicate of #382 (token-based management API).

summary: Rate limit by URI path.
evidence: Fork has per-endpoint token-bucket rate limiting (ratelimit.go); optional per-path limits are listed in ROADMAP section 1. A bounded per-(endpoint,path-prefix) bucket map answers the maintainer's memory concern. Value M, effort M.

summary: CodeQL scanning.
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yaml runs go vet and go test only. Adding a codeql.yml workflow is a standalone 20-line addition; left untouched to avoid CI changes in a triage PR. Value L-M, effort S.

summary: Authelia unreachable via domain (404).
evidence: 404 from Zoraxy means no matching proxy rule/host or default site; verify the rule hostname and the upstream scheme/port.
proposed_comment: A 404 page from Zoraxy means no proxy rule matched the requested hostname (or the rule is disabled). Check that the rule's *Matching Domain* is exactly `auth.mydomain.net`, that DNS points the name at Zoraxy, and that the target is `http://<container-ip>:9091`. Compare with the access log line for the request.

summary: Certificate for a LAN-only host.
evidence: Use the DNS challenge (does not need inbound access) or exempt the ACME path from the access rule; the ACME routing rule is evaluated before host access rules.
proposed_comment: Use the **DNS challenge** for that name (no inbound connection to the host required). The HTTP challenge path `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` is handled before the host's access rules, so it works with a LAN-only rule as long as port 80 is reachable by Let's Encrypt.

summary: Tracker: plugin system improvements.
evidence: Tracker for plugin API-key auth etc. Plugin package is being reworked elsewhere (ROADMAP section 8), nothing to verify here.

summary: Run plugins as an unprivileged user.
evidence: Plugins are started by the plugin manager as Zoraxy's user. Setting SysProcAttr.Credential on Linux is small, but the plugins package is being edited elsewhere, so not touched. Value H (security), effort S.

summary: Only accept connections from Cloudflare IPs.
evidence: Access rules evaluate the (possibly forwarded) client IP; there is no 'direct peer must be in set' rule. Needs an option to match on RemoteAddr after trusted-proxy handling. Value M, effort S-M.

summary: Sort and duplicate access rules.
evidence: UI list is unsorted (web/components/access.html) and there is no clone. Value L, effort S.

summary: Per-proxy statistics and logs view.
evidence: See #349/#596; also realtime per-host view. ROADMAP section 9 (per-upstream stats). Value M-H, effort M-L.
